findings.issue_text: [BUG] The reader thread in createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti only exits its while-loop when deletedAll is set, which happens solely after the delete forEach completes normally, so any exception thrown by a delete leaves a non-daemon thread spinning forever against the server. If any managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove() call throws (the very failure mode this suite guards against), the main test thread aborts without reaching deletedAll.set(true); the reader thread then loops indefinitely with zero backoff, and once the test framework tears the realm down every subsequent request throws and is silently swallowed into caughtExceptions, which nothing reads anymore — the forked surefire JVM carries a runaway infinite request loop for the remainder of the build (the thread is neither a daemon nor bounded by a timeout).

[ADVISORY] The test asserts caughtExceptions is empty without first joining the reader thread, so the assertion races with the thread's in-flight final iterations. The thread that is supposed to observe the concurrency defect is never quiesced before assertThat runs: an exception thrown by a groups() call that is in flight or lands after deletedAll.set(true) can be added to the CopyOnWriteArrayList after the empty() check has already passed. Because the NPE this test targets is itself a race, an intermittent reproduction occurring near the end of the delete window can be missed and the test reports green despite hitting the bug; joining the thread (or checking caughtExceptions after a latch-based stop) is the deterministic pattern.

[BUG] The fix guards only getSubGroupsCount() against the null model returned by modelSupplier.get() after a concurrent delete, while the sibling read method getSubGroupsStream() (whose signature is the enclosing context of this very hunk, line 271) and the other GroupAdapter read methods still go through getGroupModel(), which returns null in the same concurrent-delete window. A client that lists subgroups, or reads any other GroupModel property of a group being concurrently deleted, still gets the NullPointerException (HTTP 500) this PR claims to eliminate; the PR title promises a general fix for concurrent group access but only one call site of the failing pattern is patched, and the new test exercises only the top-level brief groups listing, so the remaining paths are both broken and unverified.

[BUG] createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti sets deletedAll and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader thread, so exceptions from a reader request already in flight are recorded after the assertion runs. The test can pass green while the NPE it exists to detect still occurs: the reader thread checks deletedAll only between iterations, so an HTTP call started before the flag is set completes (and adds its exception) after assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) has already evaluated; the claimed verification of the concurrency fix is unsound and will intermittently report success on a still-broken build.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is a non-daemon Thread whose while(!deletedAll.get()) loop has no termination path other than the flag, but the flag is set only after the delete loop completes on the main thread, so any exception thrown by a remove() call aborts the forEach and leaves the flag false forever. When any delete fails (which is exactly the scenario under test), the reader thread spins indefinitely issuing HTTP requests against the test server while the test method has already failed; the leaked non-daemon thread then blocks Surefire fork JVM exit and can hang the whole test run after the failure is reported.

[BUG] The concurrency fix guards only getSubGroupsCount(), but sibling methods in the same class (getSubGroupsStream is visible in this hunk's context at old line 268) follow the identical `if (isUpdated()) ...; return getGroupModel()...` pattern and still dereference getGroupModel() without a null check. A group deleted concurrently while a client iterates subgroups still NPEs through getSubGroupsStream and every other unguarded getGroupModel() call site in GroupAdapter — the PR title claims a fix for 'concurrent group access' but the class-wide invariant 'modelSupplier.get() may return null after invalidation' is enforced at exactly one method.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for a concurrently-invalidated group instead of a count, changing the method's contract from 'returns the subgroup count' to 'returns null when the backing model vanished'. Any caller that unboxes the result (e.g., long/long arithmetic, mapToLong, or a representation builder assigning to a primitive) throws NPE at the call site, so the change relocates the NullPointerException from the cache layer into callers rather than preventing it; returning 0L (or retrying the lookup) would have preserved the contract.

[BUG] The reader thread is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs, so an exception thrown by the in-flight request executing when `deletedAll.set(true)` fires is appended to the CopyOnWriteArrayList after the assertion has already evaluated. The regression test passes despite the server throwing the very NPE it is meant to catch whenever the failure lands in the final in-flight read, giving a false negative exactly in the timing window the bug lives in; the unjoined non-daemon thread can also bleed its final request into the next test's realm teardown.

[ADVISORY] The deletion of the private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement is dead-code cleanup with no traceable connection to the stated intent (fixing concurrent-access NPE) — nothing in the concurrency path or the new test involves search matching. Reviewers and bisect blame for the concurrency fix now carry an unrelated services-layer change; if the method has any remaining caller in this file that the diff does not remove, the module stops compiling. This work belongs in its own commit or PR.

[ADVISORY] Adding @Override to getRealm() is an unrelated cosmetic annotation change not traceable to the NPE-fix requirement. Pure scope noise: it signals either an interface change that is not part of this diff or a stray IDE cleanup, and it makes the concurrency fix harder to cherry-pick/backport cleanly because the cached-entity file is touched for no functional reason.

[ADVISORY] The test asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty with no tolerance for legitimate transient failures of the concurrent listing (e.g., a read that races the realm's group state in a way that surfaces an HTTP-level error), while simultaneously relying on wall-clock timing to hit the race window at all. On fast or heavily loaded CI the 100-delete loop can complete between reader iterations or the reader can hammer the server during unrelated transient errors, producing intermittent failures (or, combined with the missing join, intermittent passes) that are expensive to triage because neither outcome deterministically indicates the cache-invalidation defect.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount() returns a null Long when the concurrent delete makes modelSupplier.get() return null, where every other GroupModel implementation returns a real count and the adapter's own null-model convention elsewhere is an empty result — so 0L, not null, is the semantically correct value. Callers that unbox the result (long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) or that rely on the interface's never-null contract get a NullPointerException or a null-count leaking out through representations — i.e. the same crash class this PR claims to eliminate, just relocated to the call sites of the count method. It also creates a mixed sentinel: the isUpdated() branch returns a genuine count while the fallback can return null, so one method now answers 'real count' or 'group vanished mid-flight' with no way for callers to distinguish intent. Returning 0L (matching how a concurrently-deleted group's sub-group stream would be empty) removes the sentinel entirely.

[ADVISORY] The fix is a point patch at one accessor: the concurrent-deletion condition (modelSupplier.get() returning null) applies to every GroupAdapter accessor that dereferences the model, and only getSubGroupsCount gets the null guard in this diff. The next caller that hits the same race (group deleted between cache invalidation and a subsequent read of a stale adapter) gets the identical NullPointerException through a sibling accessor, and whoever debugs it repeats this PR's work one method at a time. The class needs a single guarded resolution point (or a central 'model gone' handling in getGroupModel()/the supplier) rather than a per-method ternary that each new accessor must remember to copy — the pattern this diff establishes is the one that produced the bug being fixed.

[BUG] The fix for the concurrent-access NPE does not prevent it but silently relocates it: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for an invalidated cache entry, and any caller that assigns to a primitive long or compares the count auto-unboxes and throws NPE at the call site under the same race. The PR's stated objective ('prevent NullPointerException') is not preserved: under the exact concurrent delete-while-read race this PR targets, callers such as admin endpoints or RealmAdapter code doing `long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()` or `count > 0` now throw an unboxing NPE instead of the original one, so the failure mode persists one frame lower and the intent silently changed from 'handle invalidation' to 'leak null through a Long-returning contract' without any evidence of human acceptance of that contract change.

[ADVISORY] The new test sets deletedAll and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader thread, so an exception thrown by an in-flight request can be appended to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed. The test can report success while the very NPE it exists to catch occurred on the reader thread after the assertion ran — a false-pass race that silently defeats the test's stated verification intent; conversely, on a failure the thread also leaks, so the diagnostic value the test was added for is not reliably delivered.

[ADVISORY] The new null-handling branch in getSubGroupsCount() — the only behavior-bearing production change in this diff — is not exercised by the added test, which only drives paginated group listing during deletes and never asserts anything about getSubGroupsCount. A regression that reverts this branch to the NPE (or changes null to 0, altering pagination counts) would pass createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, leaving the fix the PR claims to deliver unprotected by its own test.

[ADVISORY] The reader thread is a non-daemon raw Thread whose loop condition is only checked after each full admin-client call, so if the delete forEach throws (e.g., a group already removed returns an error) deletedAll is never set and the thread keeps issuing HTTP requests forever. On any failure path the thread spins unboundedly against the admin endpoint after the test has ended (and after realm teardown starts deleting resources), inflating suite runtime and causing confusing cross-test noise instead of a clean failure signal.

[BUG] The final assertion races with the reader thread: `deletedAll.set(true); assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());` executes while the reader thread may still be inside the try block, so an exception (including the NPE this test exists to detect) caught after the assertion runs is added to caughtExceptions and never observed. The test passes even when the concurrency bug reproduces: the NPE is thrown during the final in-flight read, caught at line 146 after the main thread has already asserted the list is empty, and the failure is silently dropped — giving false confidence that the fix works. The thread is never joined, so the assertion is not ordered after the last read.

[BUG] The reader thread may perform zero iterations before `deletedAll.set(true)` is reached (it is started and never joined or otherwise synchronized), so the test can pass vacuously without a single read of the groups having occurred. On a fast machine or under thread-scheduling delay, the main thread deletes all 100 groups and sets the flag before the reader thread completes even one `groups(...)` call; `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` then trivially passes and the test certifies concurrency safety while having exercised none of the concurrent read path. Nothing asserts the reader actually issued reads or saw the created groups.

[ADVISORY] The new `model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount()` branch has no test in this diff that deterministically triggers it or asserts the null return; the only modified test file (tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java) covers it, if at all, only incidentally via the racy integration test, and no unit spec for GroupAdapter/getSubGroupsCount appears in the diff. A regression that reverts the null guard or changes the null-return semantics (e.g., to 0, or to an NPE on unboxing by a caller doing `long c = getSubGroupsCount()`) is caught only when the racy integration test happens to schedule the read at the right moment — and per the race above, possibly never. The deliberate null-return behavior itself is never asserted.

[BUG] getSubGroupsCount() returns null when the cached group has been deleted concurrently, so the NPE this fix targets is relocated one frame up the stack rather than eliminated: any caller that unboxes the Long (arithmetic, comparison, intValue() when building brief group representations) throws NullPointerException on exactly the concurrent-delete race the test exercises, and REST consumers receive subGroupCount: null for a group listing instead of a count. Under the same concurrent create/delete/list load the new regression test generates, the admin group-listing path now fails with an NPE in the caller (or returns a null count in a JSON payload that previously always carried a number), so the user-facing operation still fails — it just fails in a different frame where the null is unhandled.

[ADVISORY] This is a point-fix for one delegate method: GroupAdapter contains numerous other delegating methods built on the same getGroupModel()/modelSupplier.get() pattern that the old getSubGroupsCount() used, and those siblings retain the identical unguarded NPE-on-concurrent-delete behavior this patch only removes from the count path. Any other GroupAdapter accessor (attribute reads, subgroup streams, membership lookups) invoked while the group is being deleted still dereferences a null model and throws NPE, so the class-wide race the PR title claims to fix remains reachable through paths not covered by the single-method guard; the next report of this NPE class will require another one-line patch here.
